data.name: Faraat
data.gender_notes: Faraat is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The one who carries or transports something, usually heavy items, such as a carpenter who transports wood or a boatman who transports people across a river. The name Faraat carries the meaning “Carpenter” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Faraat usually hope their child will grow to embody carpenter and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the journey of life and the challenges we face in carrying our own burdens and overcoming obstacles.
data.etymology: Faraat belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Carpenter.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Faraat total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The term "Faraat" in Islamic context is commonly used to refer to the Pharaoh who ruled over ancient Egypt during the time of Prophet Moses (peace be upon him). Pharaoh was known for his immense power, authority, and pride, making the name symbolic of power and dominance in the Arab world.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic teachings, Pharaoh Faraat is considered as a symbol of arrogance, disobedience to Allah, and disregard for human life. His story serves as a reminder for Muslims to humble themselves before Allah and avoid pride, arrogance, and disobedience, as these traits ultimately led to the downfall of Pharaoh. The name "Faraat" thus carries a spiritual significance of caution against the perils of arrogance and disobedience to Allah.
